newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends lower, December breaks 110 cents.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends lower, December breaks 110 cents.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended lower Thursday as speculative liquidation and options-related selling dragged the key December contract through the critical 110-cent level by the close, dealers said.

Prices see-sawed in negative territory throughout the session, hit by repeated rounds of profit taking by commission houses. Dealers said the market's failure to rebound after three consecutive weaker closes made buyers more cautious today.
"Nothing has changed fundamentally, but the sentiment has," said one trader.

Front-month December futures racked up the heaviest losses, hit by persistent selling of the nearby switch. Some traders cited the CSCE's decision earlier this week to raise margins on December for the second time this month.
"The impetus was the increase of the margins," said another broker. "Some people are even less willing to take a position in December."
Brisk dealings in the options ring also took its toll on the flat price, traders said. Heavy selling by both speculators and producers was noted on December 110 and 105-cent calls.

December ended down 2.30 cents at 109.90 cents a lb after trading from 109.50 to 112.10. Second-position March shed 1.05 to 102.50, compressing the nearby spread to 7.40 from 9.00 cents at the start of the week.

Technically, traders said December's settlement below 110 cents could signal a new downtrend. Sells stops were believed placed under 109.50, and then near 108.50. To the upside, resistance was seen at 111.50 and then at 114 cents.
An estimated 7,000 futures contracts were exchanged on the day, as well as nearly 3,000 options lots.
